content:
We have search results list of templates. Need the one that when applied reproduces the reaction: DIBAL-H reduction of ester to aldehyde (actually to aliphatic hydroxyl? Wait DIBAL-H reduces esters to aldehydes, but description says carbon-oxygen bond broken and another carbon-oxygen bond order changes from 2 to 1, forming aliphatic hydroxyls functional group. That sounds like reduction of ester to aldehyde? Actually aldehyde has C=O (double bond) not hydroxyl. Maybe they refer to reduction of ester to alcohol (primary alcohol) which would break C-O bond and reduce carbonyl to C-O single (hydroxyl). DIBAL-H can reduce esters to aldehydes, not alcohols unless excess. But description says forming aliphatic hydroxyls, so product is alcohol. So template likely is ester to alcohol reduction.

We need to return mapped_rxn and template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). In search results, each entry has reaction_id (maybe template_id?). The field "reaction_id" likely is template ID? Actually template catalog entries have template_id maybe same as reaction_id? The prompt says "template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash)". In search results, there is "reaction_id". Probably that's the template ID. So we need to pick the appropriate template that matches our target molecule and the described transformation.

Our target molecule SMILES: C/C(=C/[C@H]1O[C@@H](C[C@@H]2O[C@H]2/C=C/C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C)C[C@H](O)[C@H]1C)CO

This appears to be a complex molecule with an ester (C(=O)O[Si]...). The reduction would convert that ester to an alcohol (C(=O)OSi -> CH2OH?). The precursors from previous task (apply_template) gave list of possible precursors (six). Those are likely the result of applying a template that reduces the ester to an alcohol, giving different protecting group variations. So the template used there is the one we need.

Thus we need to find which template among search results corresponds to that transformation. Look at each entry's mapped_rxn: they show product and reactant. The product is the original molecule (with OH). The reactant is the ester (with OSi...). For example first entry (reaction_id 1170769) mapped_rxn shows product with [OH:29] and reactant with O=C(CP(=O)...). That's not our molecule (different). Not match.

Second entry (reaction_id 405579) seems unrelated.

Third entry (reaction_id 1037371) shows product with [OH:5] and reactant with O-C(=O)/C=C/... That's a long chain with ester. Might be similar but our molecule has a silyl ester O[Si]... not carboxylate.

Fourth entry (reaction_id 422121) shows product with [OH:46] and reactant with ...[OH:46]?? Not.

Fifth entry (reaction_id 182479) product with [OH:19] and reactant with ...[O:5][Si]... That's promising: reactant has O[Si] group. Let's inspect: product smiles: [CH3:1][CH2:2][CH2:3][C@@H:4]([O:5][Si:6]... ).../[CH:15]=[C:16](/[CH3:17])[CH2:18][OH:19] . Reactant smiles: ...[CH:15]=[O:19] . So this is reduction of carbonyl to alcohol (aldehyde to alcohol). Not ester.

Our target has an ester O[Si] attached to carbonyl: C(=O)O[Si]... So reduction of ester to alcohol would break C-O bond (the OSi) and reduce carbonyl to alcohol. That matches template where reactant has carbonyl attached to OSi and product has OH at that carbon (primary alcohol) and OSi maybe remains attached elsewhere? Actually after reduction, the OSi group would be removed (since OSi is leaving group). In product, the OSi may be attached to something else? In our target product, the OSi is still present attached to another oxygen (maybe a silyl ether elsewhere). The ester OSi is removed, leaving a primary alcohol.

Look at our target SMILES: ...C(=O)O[Si](C)(C)C(C)(C)C . So the OSi is attached to carbonyl oxygen. After reduction, that OSi would be gone, leaving CH2OH. The rest of molecule still has other OSi groups (silyl ethers). So template should convert carbonyl attached to OSi to CH2OH, breaking the C-O bond to OSi and reducing C=O to C-OH.

Which search result matches? Let's examine entry 182479: reactant has ...[CH:15]=[O:19] (aldehyde) not ester. Not.

Entry 1037371: reactant has O-C(=O)/C=C/... includes carbonyl attached to O (maybe O-). Not silyl.

Entry 1170769: reactant has O=C(CP(=O)... ) [O:29] attached to CH... not silyl.

Maybe there is a template not in top 10? Could be further down. But we can search with functional_groups_broken ["carboxylic esters"] and formed ["aliphatic hydroxyls"] gave list of 10, but none seem to match silyl ester. However maybe the template is generic for ester to alcohol reduction, not specific to silyl. The reactant side would have O-C(=O)-O (ester). In our molecule, the ester is O[Si] not O-alkyl. That's still an ester (carboxylic ester). So template should match.

Look at entry 1037371: reactant_smiles includes O-C(=O)/C=C/... and product has [OH:5] attached to carbon that was carbonyl carbon? Actually product has [OH:5] attached to carbon that was carbonyl carbon? The mapping shows product with [OH:5] and reactant with O-C(=O)... So that is ester to alcohol reduction.

Thus template_id likely 1037371? Wait reaction_id is 1037371. That seems plausible.

We need to return mapped_rxn string from that entry and template_id as integer (reaction_id). So mapped_rxn is the long string in entry 1037371.

Let's extract mapped_rxn from entry 1037371. It is:

'[CH3:1][O:2][C@@H:3]1[C@H:4]([O:5]C(=O)/C=C/C=C/C=C/C=C/C(=O)O)[CH2:6][CH2:7][C@:8]2([CH2:9][O:10]2)[C@H:11]1[C@@:12]1([CH3:13])[O:14][C@@H:15]1[CH2:16][CH:17]=[C:18]([CH3:19])[CH3:20].[OH-].[Na+].CO>>[CH3:1][O:2][C@@H:3]1[C@H:4]([OH:5])[CH2:6][CH2:7][C@:8]2([CH2:9][O:10]2)[C@H:11]1[C@@:12]1([CH3:13])[O:14][C@@H:15]1[CH2:16][CH:17]=[C:18]([CH3:19])[CH3:20]'

Check that matches our target? Our target has many silyl groups, not present. So maybe not.

But the previous apply_template gave precursors that are variations where the ester OSi is removed, leaving OH. The template used likely is generic ester reduction, which would apply to our molecule despite silyl group.

Thus we need to find which template among search results actually matches our molecule. Could test using check_smiles_reaction_template_matching tool with each template_id.

Let's try with first few IDs.
